name: Nilima Motaparti
current_role: Whole-Time Director (Commercial), Divi's Laboratories (listed on company site as Nilima Prasad Divi)
profile: Daughter of Divi's Laboratories founder Murali Divi and a major shareholder of the Hyderabad-based API maker. Joined officially in 2012 as Chief Controller (Commercial); now Whole-Time Director overseeing material sourcing and procurement, capital projects, corporate finance and investor relations.
interesting_fact: She has built Divi's sourcing strategy around a base of alternative suppliers and long-term procurement contracts to cut supply risk; she holds master's degrees in international business (GITAM) and international finance (University of Glasgow).
deep_cut_fact: She first worked at Divi's as a trainee around 1999 while still a graduate, learning finance under CFO L. Kishore Babu; she has quoted her father's advice that although the company is cash rich, 'we still need to spend and think like a small company.'
notes: Company now lists her as Nilima Prasad Divi. Low public profile; she personally oversees investor relations, so the IR route (cs@divislabs.com) is the most relevant.

name: Shao Xiaofeng
current_role: Long-time Alibaba executive (EVP and chair of the Group Risk Management Committee per FY2025 report); left the Alibaba Partnership list in June 2026, current role unclear
profile: Shao Xiaofeng (often written 邵晓锋) joined Alibaba in 2005 from the Hangzhou police, became executive president of Alipay in 2008 and Alibaba's first chief risk officer in 2012, and later served as director at Alibaba Pictures. His fortune comes mainly from his stake in Ant Group. Alibaba's FY2026 annual report (June 2026) showed him leaving the partnership.
interesting_fact: Before joining Alibaba he was a criminal investigator: head of the first brigade of the Hangzhou Public Security Bureau's criminal investigation unit; Chinese media nicknamed him Alibaba's 'old detective' gatekeeper.
deep_cut_fact: Like all Alibaba partners he has a wuxia nickname (花名): his is 'Guo Jing' (郭靖), the righteous hero of Jin Yong's novels, and staff describe him as '侠骨柔情' (chivalrous yet tender).
notes: Name commonly spelled 邵晓锋 in Chinese press (input has 邵晓峰). Very low public profile; no personal channels found. Exit from Alibaba Partnership reported by IT Home, 21 Jun 2026 (https://www.ithome.com/0/966/730.htm). Any approach would go via Alibaba/Ant corporate PR.

name: Jin Xin
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder (~40%), Dajin Heavy Industry (SZ: 002487)
profile: Jin Xin founded the predecessor of Dajin Heavy Industry in 2001; it moved from building steel structures into power-boiler steelwork (2004) and wind towers (2007) and listed in Shenzhen in 2010 as China's first A-share wind tower/pile maker. Dajin is now a leading supplier of offshore wind monopiles to Europe and is expanding into heavy-lift shipping, marshalling ports and wind-farm development.
interesting_fact: Dajin was reported as the No.1 supplier of European offshore wind monopiles by sales, with share rising from 18.5% in 2024 to 29.1% in H1 2025, and the only Asia-Pacific supplier to deliver monopiles to Europe in batches.
deep_cut_fact: He started out in 2001 at age 34 with three production lines he bought himself (H-beam, shot-blasting and colour-plate lines worth RMB 4.8m), backed by his former employer Panpan Group, which supplied RMB 8m of panels and exited a year later.
notes: Highly relevant for an energy podcast (offshore wind supply chain). Jin is non-executive chairman and keeps a low media profile; board secretary/VP Ge Xin handles investor communications. Company filed for a Hong Kong listing in Sept 2025.

name: Shintaro Yamada
current_role: Director, Representative Executive Officer and CEO, Mercari, Inc.
profile: Serial internet entrepreneur who founded Unoh (Movie Life, Photozou, Machitsuku!), sold it to Zynga in 2010, then founded Mercari in Feb 2013. Mercari became Japan's first unicorn and its dominant flea-market app, listed in 2018 (making him a billionaire), and expanded into Merpay, crypto (Mercoin) and the Kashima Antlers football club. He remains CEO.
interesting_fact: As a Waseda University student he interned at a then little-known Rakuten and built its auction site (Rakuten Auction).
deep_cut_fact: In July 2021 he set up the YAMADA Shintaro D&I Foundation with ~3 billion yen of his own money; its flagship is a no-repayment scholarship for girls choosing STEM tracks in high school, now in its 6th cohort (2026). Before Mercari he spent about six months backpacking round the world in cheap hostels.
notes: Foundation donation figure: 30億円 = ~3 billion yen (Business Insider Japan https://www.businessinsider.jp/post-239830). World-trip hostels detail: Japan Times 2016 (https://japantimes.co.jp/news/2016/03/18/business/5-night-hostels-led-japans-first-1-billion-startup, paywalled). Best route: Mercari press form or the D&I foundation.

name: Kanjibhai Virani
current_role: Co-founder, Balaji Wafers Pvt Ltd (Rajkot, Gujarat)
profile: Kanjibhai (Kanubhai) Virani co-founded Balaji Wafers with brothers Chandubhai and Bhikhubhai; the Rajkot firm grew from wafers sold at a cinema canteen into one of India's largest regional snack makers (chips, namkeen, noodles, confectionery). The family became billionaires after agreeing in Jan 2026 to sell a ~7% minority stake to General Atlantic; the next generation is increasingly running the business.
interesting_fact: The brothers began in 1974 selling wafers from the canteen of Astron Cinema in Rajkot, where they had done odd jobs; wafers were made at home until the first factory opened in 1989. Balaji is said to hold ~90% of Gujarat's chips market.
deep_cut_fact: Their first venture failed: their farmer father Popatbhai sold ancestral farmland to give the brothers Rs 20,000, which they put into farm equipment and lost, before turning to snacks.
notes: Kanjibhai is commonly listed as 'Kanubhai Virani'. Chandubhai Virani is the public face of the company; approach likely via the company. GA deal announced 22 Jan 2026 (https://www.generalatlantic.com/media-article/balaji-wafers-announces-strategic-investment-from-general-atlantic/).

name: William Clay Ford (Jr.)
current_role: Executive Chair and Chair of the Board, Ford Motor Company; vice chair, Detroit Lions
profile: Bill Ford Jr. (b. 1957), great-grandson of Henry Ford (and of Harvey Firestone), joined Ford's board in 1988, became chair in 1999 and was CEO 2001-2006; he remains Executive Chair. An early corporate environmentalist, he co-founded mobility VC firm Fontinalis Partners in 2010 and champions Ford's Michigan Central innovation hub in Detroit.
interesting_fact: He co-founded Fontinalis Partners in 2010 to back next-generation mobility start-ups, warning of 'global gridlock' as cities grow; Ford itself committed $10m to Fontinalis Capital Partners II.
deep_cut_fact: His 1979 Princeton history senior thesis was a 105-page study titled 'Henry Ford and Labor: A Reappraisal'; at Princeton he also played rugby and was president of the Ivy Club. He has been vegetarian since 1990 and a taekwondo practitioner.

public_contacts.value: ithibode@ford.com (Ian Thibodeau, Ford media contact on 2025 releases)
Directors' mail: Ford Motor Company, P.O. Box 685, Dearborn, MI 48126-0685 (published for communications to directors)

notes: Identity merge: the record mixes a 1996 Forbes listing (almost certainly his father William Clay Ford Sr., who died in 2014) with 2026 SEC insider data for Executive Chair Bill Ford Jr. Profile is for Bill Ford Jr. He bought ~$1.9m of Ford shares in Feb 2026.

name: Wang Yingmei
current_role: Chairwoman (since 2007) and General Manager (since Jul 2025), Zhejiang Yongtai Technology (SZ: 002326)
profile: Wang Yingmei is co-founder and, with He Renbao, joint actual controller of Zhejiang Yongtai Technology in Linhai/Taizhou, a fluorine-chemistry maker of pharmaceutical and crop-protection intermediates and new-energy materials such as lithium-battery electrolyte salts. She built the business from small local chemical plants in the 1990s and still runs it day to day.
interesting_fact: Yongtai describes itself as a fluorine-technology-centred maker of fluorinated pharma, crop-protection and new-energy (lithium battery) materials, with subsidiaries spanning electrolyte materials, fluorinated chips materials and lithium mining in Hainan.
deep_cut_fact: She started as a technician at Huangyan No.4 Chemical Plant (1987-92), then ran the Linhai Xingchen Chemical Plant (1992-97) and Linhai Yongli Fine Chemical Plant (1997-99) before founding Zhejiang Yongtai Chemical in 1999; she holds an EMBA and is a senior economist.
notes: Wealth shared with co-controller He Renbao. Very low media profile; board-secretary/securities office (zhengquan@) is the published route. Battery-materials angle is relevant to energy coverage.

name: Zhou Mingjie
profile: Founder and former controlling shareholder of Ocean's King Lighting (海洋王照明, SZ: 002724). Died on 16 November 2022 per the company's 2025 annual report.
notes: Deceased 16 Nov 2022 (source: Ocean's King 2025 annual report, https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2026-04-29/1225242473.PDF). Control passed to Zhou Shi and Xu Su; company set up a 'Zhou Mingjie Strivers Award Fund' in 2023 per his wishes. The 2026 Forbes real-time entry likely reflects heirs.

name: Yu Kai
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Horizon Robotics (HKEX: 9660)
profile: AI scientist (Nanjing University, PhD LMU Munich) who worked at Siemens and NEC Labs America, then founded Baidu's Institute of Deep Learning and its autonomous-driving project before co-founding Horizon Robotics in 2015. Horizon makes driving-assistance chips and software (Journey processors) used by VW, BYD, Hyundai and others, and listed in Hong Kong in Oct 2024 in that year's largest HK IPO.
interesting_fact: At Baidu (2012-15) he founded and led the Institute of Deep Learning, Baidu's autonomous-driving team and the PaddlePaddle deep-learning platform; earlier he directed NEC Labs America's media lab, a pioneer of convolutional neural networks.
deep_cut_fact: In 2011 he was an adjunct faculty member at Stanford, teaching a graduate-level class in the Computer Science Department; his NEC group is also credited with first place in the inaugural ImageNet challenge (2010).
notes: Strong fit for a tech/data-center podcast (AI chips, energy-efficient computing). Frequent conference speaker (WEF profile: https://weforum.org/people/yu-kai). IR email surfaced via search of the IR page (page is JS-rendered; not re-verified by direct fetch).

name: Jenny Zhiya Qian
current_role: Co-founder, Cotti Coffee (库迪咖啡); founder and former CEO of Luckin Coffee
profile: Qian Zhiya (钱治亚) worked for over a decade alongside Lu Zhengyao in the CAR Inc./UCAR group, rising to UCAR COO, then founded Luckin Coffee in 2017 and took it public on Nasdaq in 2019. After leaving Luckin in 2020, she and Lu launched Cotti Coffee in 2022, which expanded rapidly to thousands of stores at home and abroad.
interesting_fact: Cotti Coffee, founded in 2022, reportedly reached about 5,000 outlets within its first couple of years, sparking a price war with Luckin and Starbucks in China.
deep_cut_fact: A 2018 profile noted she personally drinks around three to five cups of coffee a day.
notes: Sensitive: she was removed as Luckin CEO after its 2020 fabricated-sales scandal. Avoid in outreach. Very private; no personal channels found. Cotti's own site did not expose a contact address; best route is Cotti corporate PR.

name: Charles Beauduin
current_role: Chairman of Barco NV (since Sept 2024); CEO and owner of Vandewiele NV (since 1993)
profile: Belgian industrialist (b. 1959; law, KU Leuven; MBA, Harvard) from a former sugar-industry family. He took over Kortrijk-based textile-machinery maker Vandewiele in 1993 and built it into a ~4,000-person group in 14 countries (incl. Italy's Savio, bought 2021). Barco director since 2015, he was co-CEO 2021-2024 and is now chairman; he owns ~25% of Barco.
interesting_fact: Vandewiele invests about 10% of sales in R&D; Beauduin says its looms went from one motor per machine to 14,000 computer-controlled motors, with AI that lets machines learn to solve problems: 'We've become a technology company.'
deep_cut_fact: Vandewiele, started some 165 years ago as a loom builder, now lists energy efficiency (in its own plants and in the machines it ships) as its current focus, and a single modern loom can cost close to EUR 2 million.
notes: Chairmanship announced Jun 2024 (https://www.barco.com/en/about/press-releases/2024/charles-beauduin-becomes-chairman-of-barco). Known in Belgian press for his 'legendary optimism'. Barco data-center/visualisation and Vandewiele energy-efficiency angles fit the podcast.

name: Kim Hyun-tae
current_role: CEO (management division) and largest shareholder, Voronoi Inc. (KOSDAQ: 310210), Incheon, South Korea
profile: Former securities-industry asset manager (eBest, Hanwha and KB Securities) who took over Songdo-based AI-driven drug developer Voronoi in 2016, a year after his younger brother founded it, and listed it on KOSDAQ in 2022. He runs the business side while his brother leads research; lead cancer drugs VRN10 and VRN11 entered Phase 1 in 2025.
interesting_fact: Voronoi's VRN11, a next-gen EGFR lung-cancer drug, showed complete disappearance of brain metastases in some patients in 2026 Phase 1 data, presented at WCLC 2026 in Seoul.
notes: Korean press refers to him as 김현태 공동대표/경영부문 대표; research CEO is Kim Dae-kwon (김대권), likely the brother Forbes calls Hyun-seok. ~38% stake reported in 2024. Low English-language profile.

name: Evan Sharp
current_role: Founding CEO, West Co. (The Workshop for Emotional and Spiritual Technology PBC), San Francisco
profile: Co-founder and long-time chief design & creative officer of Pinterest, which he built as a side project while a designer at Facebook. He left full-time Pinterest work in 2021 (briefly joining Jony Ive's LoveFrom), and now runs West Co., a public-benefit startup co-founded with Biz Stone that raised a $29m seed led by Spark Capital and makes Tangle, an 'intentional living' social app.
interesting_fact: West Co.'s first app, Tangle (invite-only, late 2025), asks users each day 'What's your intention for today?'; the company draws on religious and communal rituals and has a 'Founding Ancient Technologist' on its team.
deep_cut_fact: He studied architecture at Columbia but never finished; he says 'Because I had never finished architecture school, I had felt like I'd never truly learned my design craft' and that at Facebook 'all I wanted to do was go work on Pinterest.'
notes: Active angel investor. Best route: West Co. (hello@west.co). Funding coverage: https://www.pymnts.com/news/social-commerce/2026/twitter-and-pinterest-vets-pitch-new-social-app-tangle/

name: Douglas Fregin
current_role: Founder & Managing Partner, Quantum Valley Investments (Waterloo, Ontario)
profile: Electrical engineer (University of Windsor) who co-founded Research In Motion (BlackBerry) in 1984 with his grade-school friend Mike Lazaridis, designing early circuit boards and serving as VP of operations until retiring in 2007. In 2013 the pair launched Quantum Valley Investments with $100m of their own money to commercialise quantum information science; he was an early $10m donor to the Perimeter Institute.
interesting_fact: RIM's first product, the 'Budgie', was shown by Fregin and Lazaridis at Fairview Park Mall in Kitchener in 1984; the start-up was helped by a $15,000 Ontario New Ventures loan in 1985.
deep_cut_fact: Long before BlackBerry, he shared a 1994 Technology & Engineering Emmy (with Eastman Kodak and the National Film Board of Canada) for developing a keycode reader; RIM's DigiSync film reader also earned an Academy technical achievement award.
notes: Known as 'the other RIM guy' (Canadian Business, 2005) - keeps a much lower profile than Lazaridis. Best route: Quantum Valley Investments contact form. Quantum/computing angle fits a data-center podcast.

name: Lucia Borges Maggi
current_role: Principal shareholder and board adviser, Amaggi Group (Brazil)
profile: Lúcia Borges Maggi (in her 90s, born in Rio Grande do Sul) co-founded Sementes Maggi with her husband André Maggi in São Miguel do Iguaçu, Paraná, in 1977; it grew into Amaggi, one of Brazil's largest grain, logistics and energy agribusinesses, centred in Mato Grosso. After André's death in 2001 she became the main shareholder; she keeps an advisory seat on the board and has been ranked by Forbes as Brazil's richest woman.
interesting_fact: Amaggi began in 1977 as a seed business, Sementes Maggi, in São Miguel do Iguaçu (Paraná), before expanding into Mato Grosso and becoming an agribusiness, river-logistics and energy group.
deep_cut_fact: The family's philanthropy runs through the Fundação André e Lúcia Maggi (28 years of history), whose flagship 'Crescendo com o Local' programme backs family farming, local entrepreneurship and job training in Amaggi's regions, e.g. machine-operator courses in Itacoatiara (AM).
notes: Very private, elderly (~94 per Nov 2026 press, https://www.correio24horas.com.br/em-alta/bilionaria-brasileira-de-94-anos-comecou-do-zero-e-ajudou-a-construir-gigante-do-agronegocio-1126); unlikely guest. Son Blairo Maggi (ex-agriculture minister) is the family's public face. Avoid family-estate dispute topics.

name: Dinesh Chandra Agarwal
current_role: Founder, Managing Director and CEO, IndiaMART InterMESH Ltd
profile: Computer-science graduate of HBTI Kanpur who worked at CMC, C-DOT and HCL (moving to the US in 1992), then quit after India launched public internet in Aug 1995 to start IndiaMART from a house in Patparganj, Delhi, in 1996 with ~Rs 40,000 seed money. IndiaMART pivoted from exporters to Indian MSMEs, listed in 2019, and dominates India's online B2B marketplace.
interesting_fact: He decided to quit HCL in the US the day India announced public internet access (15 Aug 1995); IndiaMART began as an online directory of Indian exporters and now claims ~60% of India's online B2B marketplace.
deep_cut_fact: He comes from a trading family in Nanpara (UP), which he credits for keeping him grounded; his two favourite books are Freakonomics and Sun Tzu's Art of War, he looks forward to TiE's annual global retreats, and he supports Olympic Gold Quest.
notes: Very accessible: active on X and LinkedIn, frequent podcast guest (e.g. Founder Thesis) and TiE mentor; best route is a short DM/LinkedIn message referencing MSME digitisation.

name: Ian Wace
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Marshall Wace (London hedge fund); co-founder of the education charity Ark
profile: British financier (b. 1963) who joined S.G. Warburg without a university degree, ran European equity sales and proprietary trading there, then headed equity and derivatives trading at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell before co-founding Marshall Wace with Paul Marshall in 1997. The firm grew into one of Europe's largest hedge funds; he also co-founded and later chaired the charity Ark (Absolute Return for Kids).
interesting_fact: He became S.G. Warburg's youngest-ever director at age 25, despite having no college degree.
deep_cut_fact: In 2017 he bought Tanera Mòr, the largest of the Summer Isles off north-west Scotland, and has been developing it as an eco-minded retreat for up to 60 guests (profiled by the FT in June 2025 as a 'radical vision for a remote Scottish island').
notes: Private; do not raise his family history (1994 family loss) or political donations. Media requests go via Boscobel & Partners. Ark chair appointment 2010: https://arkonline.org/news/ian-wace-takes-chairmanship

name: Geetanjali Vikram Kirloskar
current_role: Chairperson and Managing Director, Kirloskar Systems (holding/partner company for the Toyota Kirloskar JVs)
profile: Geetanjali Kirloskar leads Kirloskar Systems, the Bengaluru holding company behind the Toyota Kirloskar Motor and related Toyota joint ventures plus textile machinery, auto components and logistics. She took over the group with her daughter after Vikram Kirloskar's death in 2022, and co-chairs the India-Japan Trade & Business Council and the CII Centre for Green Mobility.
interesting_fact: She co-chairs the CII Centre for Green Mobility, set up the India Japan Council for India's Ministry of External Affairs, and sits on the board of the Rhode Island School of Design (US).
deep_cut_fact: She is Honorary Consul of Finland in Karnataka and was made a Knight First Class of Finland's Order of the Lion in Dec 2022; she also founded a Kirloskar scholarship for Japanese-language training at Bangalore City University. Before industry she had a 'parallel life from acting to advertising'.
notes: No published contact found for Kirloskar Systems; route via Toyota Kirloskar Motor corporate communications or CII Centre for Green Mobility. Green-mobility/EV angle fits the energy podcast. 2026 interview: https://www.outlookbusiness.com/corporate/womens-day-2026-you-cant-push-for-respect-it-comes-from-hard-work-says-kirloskar-systems-geetanjali-kirloskar

name: Yi Feng (Feng Yi)
current_role: Director and Vice President (副总经理), Sangfor Technologies (SZ: 300454); one of three co-controlling founders
profile: Feng Yi (b. 1974) is one of the three ex-ZTE engineers (with He Chaoxi and Xiong Wu) who founded Shenzhen-based Sangfor Technologies in December 2000. Sangfor grew from VPN appliances into cybersecurity, hyper-converged infrastructure and cloud/data-center products, listing in Shenzhen in 2018; Feng has served as director and head of management engineering and is now director and VP.
interesting_fact: Sangfor is one of China's leading suppliers of hyper-converged infrastructure (HCI) used to build distributed cloud data centers, alongside its cybersecurity business.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated from the University of Science and Technology of China in 1998 with a double bachelor's in automatic control and economic management, and spent just two years doing R&D at ZTE before co-founding Sangfor in Dec 2000.
notes: Name order: Chinese name 冯毅 = Feng Yi (Forbes lists as 'Yi Feng'). Low public profile; data-center/HCI angle fits the podcast. Approach via Sangfor IR.

name: Jerry Ng
current_role: Founder and President Commissioner (chairman), PT Bank Jago Tbk (IDX: ARTO); major shareholder of BFI Finance Indonesia
profile: Veteran Indonesian banker with 30+ years at Bank Central Asia, Bank Danamon and Bank BTPN (president director until 2019) and former deputy chair of IBRA. In late 2019 he bought control of small Bank Artos and rebuilt it as digital Bank Jago (with Gojek and GIC as partners), which had 20.1m customers and rising profits by mid-2026.
interesting_fact: At BTPN he is credited with conceiving Jenius, one of Indonesia's pioneering digital-banking apps, years before launching Bank Jago.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Pontianak, West Kalimantan, he is a trustee of the Blum Center for Developing Economies at UC Berkeley, reflecting his long interest in banking for the 'mass market' and micro-entrepreneurs.

public_contacts.value: https://www.jago.com/en/media-center (Corporate Communication contact on press releases)

notes: Blum Center trusteeship per Forbes profile facts (https://www.forbes.com/profile/jerry-ng/). July 2026 reports said he was exploring a partial sale/strategic investor for BFI and Bank Jago (https://www.caproasia.com/?p=77076). Jago press-release emails are obfuscated; use media center.
